nodes.description: Mitochondrial protein quality control in the inner membrane is carried out by the m-AAA protease, whose subunits are AFG3L2 and paraplegin (SPG7). Both of this entry's mitochondrial subtypes are defects of that one complex, which is why they are modelled at a single node: in the SPAX5 subtype, biallelic AFG3L2 dysfunction causes mitochondrial proteotoxic stress and activates the OMA1-DELE1-HRI integrated stress response pathway, and SPG7-associated disease is the paraplegin-subunit counterpart. The integrated-stress-response detail below is established for the AFG3L2 arm specifically.

evidence.reference_title: Sustained OMA1-mediated integrated stress response is beneficial for spastic ataxia type 5
evidence.snippet: In this work, we demonstrated that mitochondrial proteotoxicity in the absence/mutation of AFG3L2 activates the OMA1-DELE1-HRI pathway eliciting the integrated stress response.

evidence.reference_title: Concurrent AFG3L2 and SPG7 mutations associated with syndromic parkinsonism and optic atrophy with aberrant OPA1 processing and mitochondrial network fragmentation.
evidence.snippet: Mutations in the m-AAA subunits AFG3L2 and paraplegin are associated with autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxia (SCA28) and autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG7), respectively.

nodes.description: In paradigmatic SPAX disorders, especially ARSACS, widespread white matter damage with secondary demyelination contributes to the spastic-ataxic phenotype. Only SACS is bound here: the PROSPAX comparison cited below found this pattern in ARSACS but explicitly not in SPG7 patients, so binding SPG7 to this node would contradict the entry's own evidence.
nodes.id: White Matter Degeneration and Secondary Demyelination

evidence.reference_title: An MRI evaluation of white matter involvement in paradigmatic forms of spastic ataxia: results from the multi-center PROSPAX study
evidence.snippet: In ARSACS, but not SPG7 patients, we observed a complex and multi-faced involvement of brain WM, with a clinically meaningful widespread loss of axonal and dendritic integrity, secondary demyelination and, overall, a reduction in cellularity and volume.
